reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it promotes Texas Roadhouse appetizers, catering, and restaurant ordering for March Madness gatherings. Its discussion of the mobile app, profile creation, email or text lists, rewards, and a $5 coupon is framed as ordinary restaurant loyalty and food-purchase information rather than a wealth-return promise, credential request, or other scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Texas Roadhouse have plenty of appetizers that will be a slam dunk when it comes to feeding your family and friends.
You can download our mobile app either with an iPhone or an Android.
Yes, we have a new 2020 catering menu.
Come and get some appetizers and take them home.
Just for downloading the app and creating a profile, you get a free appetizer for your next visit.

opening.argument: The segment links an immediate reward to a low-effort registration action: viewers are told that downloading the mobile app and creating a profile produces a free appetizer. It then adds further incentives for joining email and text lists, including birthday and anniversary appetizers. That is a direct solicitation to provide personal participation in exchange for benefits, presented as easy and automatic. The food discussion supplies the promotional setting, but it does not remove the central promise-action structure: install, create a profile, or enroll in messaging, and receive something of value. The viewer is being moved into an account and contact funnel through attractive rewards rather than simply informed about menu items.

citations.quote: Just for downloading the app and creating a profile, you get a free appetizer for your next visit.
If you sign up for emails, you will get all kinds of different coupons.
If you text in and get on our text list, they'll send you birthday appetizers.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the offer ordinary restaurant loyalty does not answer the specific linkage. The segment expressly ties profile creation to a free appetizer and separately ties email and text enrollment to incentives. Describing the reward as a coupon or appetizer does not establish that the acquisition and contact process is transparent, limited, or risk-free.

citations.quote: Just for downloading the app and creating a profile, you get a free appetizer for your next visit.
If you sign up for emails, you will get all kinds of different coupons.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted reward is a restaurant appetizer, not cash, an investment return, or an asset withdrawal. The evidence also identifies the concrete action and ordinary context: download the restaurant app, create a profile, and use the benefit on a next visit. Nothing shows hidden fees, credential theft, or a deceptive claim about what the viewer will receive.

citations.quote: you get a free appetizer for your next visit.
You can download our mobile app either with an iPhone or an Android.

opening.argument: Several incentives are stacked around digital enrollment and payment: a free appetizer for creating a profile, coupons or incentives for email registration, birthday and anniversary appetizers for text subscribers, and a $5 coupon for paying through the mobile app. The accumulation makes the offer look unusually easy and rewarding while encouraging multiple forms of participation and an online payment pathway. Even if each individual benefit resembles a promotion, the combined presentation conditions viewers to install, register, surrender contact access, and pay through the same channel. The segment gives no qualifying details about eligibility, expiration, or restrictions, so the repeated certainty of these benefits is a meaningful warning sign.

citations.quote: Just for downloading the app and creating a profile, you get a free appetizer for your next visit.
If you text in and get on our text list, they'll send you birthday appetizers.
If you pay with your mobile app, you get a $5 coupon.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense recites the same promotional claims without addressing their accumulation or the missing conditions. A visible food setting does not explain why profile creation, email enrollment, text enrollment, and mobile payment are each paired with incentives. The segment's upbeat tone can make the benefits sound guaranteed while leaving material limitations unstated.

citations.quote: If you sign up for emails, you will get all kinds of different coupons.
If you pay with your mobile app, you get a $5 coupon.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Multiple loyalty benefits do not become scam indicators merely by being listed together. The amounts and forms are modest restaurant benefits, and the evidence describes ordinary app functions such as ordering, payment, gift-card balance checking, and wait-list access. The absence of stated restrictions is not evidence that restrictions were falsely concealed.

citations.quote: You can check your gift card balance.
You can get on the wait list from home

opening.argument: Although presented as a casual television food segment, the content functions as a coordinated customer-acquisition pitch. The host repeatedly directs viewers to order through the app, create a profile, join email or text lists, pay online, and visit the named restaurants. The guests supply enthusiastic endorsements and a sequence of rewards, while the closing supplies the website and two locations. That is more than neutral information about appetizers: it steers viewers toward a chain of actions that can unlock benefits and bring them into an ongoing marketing relationship. The cooking-show setting and friendly dialogue therefore operate as persuasive packaging for the enrollment offer.

citations.quote: Come and get some appetizers and take them home.
You can create a profile, and you can start unlocking rewards.
If you need more information, check out TexasRoadhouse.com.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the segment's commercial purpose as exculpatory, but that is the point at issue. Calling it restaurant information does not negate the repeated calls to order, enroll, unlock rewards, and use the website. The format makes those calls feel like friendly editorial advice rather than an overt solicitation.

citations.quote: Download our mobile app. You can order right. Off your phone
If you need more information, check out TexasRoadhouse.com.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The video openly identifies what it is promoting: appetizers, takeout, catering, and restaurant services. Its calls to action lead to food purchases and a disclosed loyalty program, not an anonymous payment destination or promise of financial gain. The website and restaurant locations reinforce ordinary commerce rather than conceal it.
